slice: WI-3dbb44 fast-local-fleet slice 5 (5a engine PCM callback + 5b worker forwarding). Slice 5c host playback not included.

what_this_measures.ttfa: Host wall time from writing the synthesize request to holding the first chunk's PCM bytes. Stage A has no separate TTFA: the single blob is the whole utterance, so ttfa == wall by construction.
what_this_measures.rtf: synthesis wall / audio duration. >1.0 is slower than realtime.
what_this_measures.underruns: warm-bench replays playback from the recorded chunk arrival times: the player starts at the first chunk and consumes in realtime; every later chunk that lands after the buffer would have run dry counts as one underrun. n=15 runs per configuration.
what_this_measures.p95: reported as the observed max, the honest ceiling at n=15 (same convention as F8-qwen-tts-cuda-2026-08-27.json).

ship_gate.criteria: p50 TTFA < 500 ms AND p95 TTFA < 1 s AND RTF < 1.0 with zero underruns on a multi-sentence fixture

verdict.cuda_0.6b: PASS at every chunk size measured (12, 8, 6 frames). Default chunk 12: TTFA p50 435 ms, p95 441 ms, RTF max 0.571, 0 underruns over 15 runs.
verdict.metal_0.6b: FAIL. TTFA improves 6.1 s -> 1.29 s but RTF gets *worse* (1.40 -> 1.66 median) and playback underruns 120 times over 15 runs. Do not enable streaming on Metal without a pre-buffer; see metal_prebuffer_note.

metal_prebuffer_note.worked_example: F5_paragraph on Metal streams at RTF 1.669 for 23.26 s of audio, so a player must hold 23.26 * 0.669 = 15.6 s before starting or it runs dry. That makes the effective time-to-first-audio ~16 s, not the 1.29 s the TTFA column shows. Reporting the 1.29 s alone would be dishonest.
metal_prebuffer_note.why_metal_regresses: Streaming forces chunked vocoder decode. On CUDA that is already the default for utterances over 34 frames, so streaming costs little. On Metal the default is one graph for the whole utterance, and paying per-chunk graph build/alloc 25 times (plus re-decoding 12 context frames per chunk) costs more than it saves. Metal decode went 4.77 s -> 9.73 s on the 180-frame CLI fixture.
metal_prebuffer_note.levers_not_taken: A larger QWEN3_TTS_DECODER_GPU_CONTEXT_FRAMES makes each chunk more faithful but slower; a smaller chunk lowers TTFA and raises RTF further (Metal chunk 4: TTFA 471 ms, RTF 2.385, 28 underruns on one F4 run). Neither closes the Metal RTF gap. Kokoro remains the fast mouth on Metal.

build.harness: cmd/warm-bench -stream (schema qwen.warmbench.v1), same five fixtures / warmup discard / RTF definition as F7 and F8

cuda_stage_a.note: Baseline. TTFA equals full wall; zero underruns is trivially true because playback cannot start until the whole utterance exists.

cuda_stage_b_chunk12.note: Engine default chunk size. Best throughput headroom of the three.

cuda_stage_b_chunk6.note: Lowest TTFA measured, still under the RTF gate. The curve is monotone: halving the chunk roughly halves TTFA and adds ~0.1 to RTF.

metal_stage_a.note: Baseline. Already above realtime before streaming is involved.

metal_stage_b_chunk12.note: Fails all four criteria. This is the honest result: streaming is not a Metal speed win.

equivalence_checks.method: qwen3-tts-cli, greedy sampling (temperature 0 — the only deterministic mode, since rng_ is seeded from std::random_device), --max-tokens 180, byte comparison of the output WAVs. Greedy never emits EOS on this model, which is why the frame count is capped.

metal.streamed_vs_single_graph_decode: DIFFERS — 14.6 dB SNR, max abs diff 0.087 full scale. This is the pre-existing chunked-decode approximation (12 frames of left context), not an artifact of interleaving. It is the shipped CUDA default; on Metal, opting into streaming opts into it.
metal.chunk_boundary_discontinuity: none: max sample-to-sample step at the 14 chunk seams was 351 (int16), against a p99 step of 1097 and a peak step of 10435 elsewhere in the same signal. No clicks.

defaults_not_flipped: Engine: with no PCM callback installed the whole-utterance path runs unchanged, byte-identical to pin 22277bc (verified on both backends).
Worker: stage A remains the default. Streaming needs "stream":true per request or QWEN3_TTS_STREAM=1.
obey-voice: untouched by these PRs. It never sets "stream", so it keeps receiving one blob per utterance.
